subject: Geography
description: Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna, Cauvery, Narmada, Tapi systems

questions.stem: The LONGEST river of PENINSULAR India (entirely within India) is:

options.option_text: Mahanadi, of Odisha and Chhattisgarh
Godavari, the 'Dakshin Ganga'
Krishna, of Andhra and Maharashtra
Cauvery, of Karnataka and Tamil Nadu

questions.explanation: GODAVARI — longest peninsular river (~1465 km). Source: TRYAMBAKESHWAR, Nashik district, Maharashtra (Western Ghats). Drains into BAY OF BENGAL via Andhra Pradesh delta. Called 'DAKSHIN GANGA' (Ganga of the South) due to its size + sanctity. Tributaries: PRANHITA (largest; itself formed by Wardha + Wainganga), Indravati, Sabari, Manjira. KUMBH MELA at Nashik on its banks. Krishna ~ 1400 km, Cauvery ~ 800 km, Mahanadi ~ 850 km. Total drainage: 312,800 km² (largest peninsular basin).
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The NARMADA + TAPI rivers are unique because they:

options.option_text: Originate in Western Ghats and flow east
Flow WEST into Arabian Sea (rift valleys)
Are the only rain-fed rivers in India
Rise from Himalayan glaciers and flow south

questions.explanation: Most peninsular rivers flow EAST into Bay of Bengal (because Western Ghats are higher → eastern slope is gentler). Exceptions: NARMADA + TAPI flow WEST into Arabian Sea via the GULF OF KHAMBHAT. Both flow through RIFT VALLEYS — not classical river valleys but tectonic depressions. NARMADA between Vindhya (north) + Satpura (south); TAPI between Satpura (north) + Ajanta hills (south). Hence these don't form deltas — they form ESTUARIES at their mouths. Narmada source: AMARKANTAK (Maikal hills, MP). Tapi source: MULTAI (Betul, MP).
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The CAUVERY river originates at TALA CAUVERY in:

options.option_text: Tamil Nadu, where the river ends
Brahmagiri Hills (Coorg, Karnataka)
Andhra Pradesh, eastern region
Kerala, far south of the country

questions.explanation: CAUVERY (Kaveri) — sacred river of South India. Source: TALA CAUVERY at BRAHMAGIRI HILLS in KODAGU (Coorg) district, Karnataka (Western Ghats). Length ~800 km. Flows through Karnataka + Tamil Nadu, drains into BAY OF BENGAL via Poompuhar (TN delta). Famous tributaries: HEMAVATI, KABINI, BHAVANI, AMARAVATI. Forms SHIVANASAMUDRA waterfall (Karnataka) — second largest in Asia by volume. Cauvery WATER DISPUTE between Karnataka + Tamil Nadu — long-running, settled by SC awards (last major: 2018, set state shares). Kallanai / GRAND ANICUT — ancient Chola dam on Cauvery, still functional.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: MAHANADI's largest tributary on the LEFT bank is:

options.option_text: Tel, on the right bank of river
Seonath, the largest left-bank tributary
Indravati, joining the Godavari only
Bhima, which is in Krishna basin

questions.explanation: MAHANADI — origin: Sihawa range in Chhattisgarh. ~850 km long. Drains Chhattisgarh + Odisha; ends in DELTA on Bay of Bengal (Paradip area). Major dam: HIRAKUD (Odisha; one of world's longest earthen dams, opened 1957 by Nehru). Tributaries — LEFT bank: SEONATH (largest), Hasdeo, Mand, Ib; RIGHT bank: Ong, Tel, Jonk. 'Mahanadi' = Great River. Used to be 'Sorrow of Odisha' (frequent floods), now controlled by Hirakud.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The KRISHNA river originates at MAHABALESHWAR. Its largest tributary by water-yield is:

options.option_text: Bhima, joining at Raichur in Karnataka
Tungabhadra, joining at Sangameshwaram
Koyna, the small Maharashtrian river
Musi, flowing through Hyderabad city

questions.explanation: KRISHNA — second-longest peninsular river (~1400 km). Source: MAHABALESHWAR (Maharashtra, Western Ghats). Drains Maharashtra → Karnataka → Telangana → Andhra Pradesh → Bay of Bengal (Krishna delta). Tributaries: TUNGABHADRA (largest by water yield; itself formed by Tunga + Bhadra in Karnataka); BHIMA (longest tributary, ~860 km); KOYNA, GHATAPRABHA, MALAPRABHA, MUSI (Hyderabad), KUNDALI. Major dams: Almatti (Karnataka), Srisailam (AP-TG border), Nagarjuna Sagar (AP-TG border). Krishna water dispute among 4 states.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: Peninsular rivers are mostly RAIN-FED, leading to:

options.option_text: Year-round perennial flow always
Seasonal flow with low summer levels
Wide variability in salinity yearly
Fast erosion of new mountain ranges

questions.explanation: Peninsular rivers — rain-fed (no glacier source like Himalayan rivers). Flow varies seasonally with monsoon — high in monsoon, low (sometimes nearly dry) in summer. Many smaller streams dry up entirely. This restricts navigation, hydropower reliability, irrigation. Hence many DAMS (Hirakud, Nagarjuna Sagar, Tungabhadra, Mettur) for water storage. Compare with Himalayan rivers (perennial, glacier-fed). Western Ghats rivers also have higher slopes → more erosion + waterfalls (Jog Falls, Sivasamudram, Hogenakkal).
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: Match: NAGARJUNA SAGAR DAM, one of India's largest masonry dams, is on the:

options.option_text: Godavari river in Andhra Pradesh
Krishna river (AP-Telangana border)
Cauvery river in Tamil Nadu state
Mahanadi river in Odisha state

questions.explanation: NAGARJUNA SAGAR DAM — masonry dam on KRISHNA river, on AP-Telangana border. Built 1955-67. Length 4137 ft, height 124 m. Forms NAGARJUNA SAGAR LAKE (3rd largest man-made lake in world by volume at one time). Named for ancient Buddhist site Nagarjunakonda nearby (now mostly submerged; key relics moved to a museum on a hill). Major dams in peninsula: HIRAKUD (Mahanadi, longest earthen dam), SARDAR SAROVAR (Narmada, Gujarat — 4th tallest concrete-gravity dam in world), TUNGABHADRA (Tungabhadra), METTUR (Cauvery), KOYNA (Koyna), ALMATTI (Krishna), SRIRAM SAGAR (Godavari).
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Godavari river, also called 'Vriddha Ganga' (Old Ganga), originates at Trimbakeshwar. In which district of Maharashtra is this origin point located?

options.option_text: Satara district on the Mahabaleshwar plateau, Maharashtra
Kodagu (Coorg) district in the Brahmagiri Hills, Karnataka
Nashik district in the northern Western Ghats, Maharashtra
Betul district in the Satpura ranges, Madhya Pradesh

questions.explanation: Trimbakeshwar, a pilgrimage town, lies in Nashik district of Maharashtra and is the source of the Godavari — India's second-longest river. Option A (Satara/Mahabaleshwar) is where the Krishna originates; Option B (Brahmagiri Hills, Kodagu) is where the Cauvery originates; Option D (Satpura/Betul) is associated with the Narmada's headwaters. Candidates frequently mix up these Western Ghats and Satpura origins.

questions.stem: The Tungabhadra river, on whose banks the UNESCO World Heritage city of Hampi flourished, is formed by the confluence of the Tunga and Bhadra rivers. At which place in Karnataka do these two rivers meet?

options.option_text: Hampi in Ballari district of Karnataka, near Hospet city
Kudali in Shivamogga (Shimoga) district of Karnataka
Bidar in Bidar district of north Karnataka state
Gadag in Gadag district of north Karnataka state

questions.explanation: The Tunga and Bhadra rivers — both originating on the Gangamoola peak in Chikmagalur district — join at Kudali (Koodli) near Shivamogga to form the Tungabhadra. Option A (Hampi) is a famous site ON the Tungabhadra, not its origin. Bidar and Gadag are in northern Karnataka and have no connection to this confluence. Kudali is a significant Shaivite pilgrimage site precisely because of this river confluence.

questions.stem: The Indravati river, a right-bank tributary of the Godavari that harbours the Indravati National Park (home to wild buffaloes), forms the natural boundary between Chhattisgarh and which state in its lower course before emptying into the Godavari?

options.option_text: Odisha (through Malkangiri and Koraput districts)
Telangana (through Bhadradri Kothagudem district)
Maharashtra (through Gadchiroli district boundary)
Andhra Pradesh (through Alluri Sitharama Raju district)

questions.explanation: Although the Indravati originates in Kalahandi district of Odisha, it flows westward through the Bastar region of Chhattisgarh and then turns south, forming the Chhattisgarh–Maharashtra boundary through Gadchiroli district before joining the Godavari. Option A (Odisha) is where it originates, not where it forms a boundary. Options B and D (Telangana, Andhra Pradesh) are downstream of the Indravati–Godavari junction, not bordering the Indravati.

questions.stem: The spectacular Hogenakkal Falls, colloquially called the 'Niagara of India,' descends from the Deccan Plateau into the plains. On which river and in which district is it located?

options.option_text: Tungabhadra river, near Hassan district in Karnataka
Penna river, near Chittoor district in Andhra Pradesh
Bhavani river, near Erode district in Tamil Nadu
Cauvery river, near Dharmapuri district in Tamil Nadu

questions.explanation: Hogenakkal (meaning 'smoking rocks' in Kannada) is on the Cauvery river in Dharmapuri district, Tamil Nadu, where the river drops sharply at the Karnataka–Tamil Nadu boundary. Option C (Bhavani near Erode) is the most tempting distractor because the Bhavani is a major Cauvery tributary in Tamil Nadu and the region has other falls; but the Bhavani does not produce the Hogenakkal Falls. Tungabhadra (A) is a Krishna tributary in Karnataka; Penna (B) is a separate east-flowing river.

questions.stem: Polavaram Irrigation Project, declared a National Project in 2014 and designed to divert Godavari waters to benefit Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, and Chhattisgarh, is under construction in which district of Andhra Pradesh?

options.option_text: Krishna river, in Vijayawada (NTR) district of AP
Godavari river, in Eluru (West Godavari) district of AP
Penna river, in Nellore (SPSR Nellore) district of AP
Godavari river, in Kakinada (East Godavari) district of AP

questions.explanation: Polavaram Project (also called Indira Sagar Project) is on the Godavari river in Eluru district (formerly West Godavari). Option D is a very common error — East Godavari district is also on the Godavari, but the project site is in Eluru/West Godavari. Option A is wrong on river identity (Krishna, not Godavari); Option C involves a completely different river, the Penna, which flows further south.

questions.stem: The Amarkantak plateau in Madhya Pradesh is geographically unique because it simultaneously gives rise to three river systems flowing in entirely different directions. Which option correctly identifies all three?

options.option_text: Narmada flowing west, Mahanadi flowing east, and Betwa flowing north
Tapi flowing west, Wainganga flowing south, and Pench flowing north-east
Narmada flowing west, Son flowing north-east, and Johilla flowing north
Chambal flowing north, Betwa flowing north-east, and Ken flowing east

questions.explanation: Amarkantak is the trifurcating point of the Narmada (flows west into Arabian Sea), Son (flows north-east to join the Ganga), and the Johilla (a Son tributary flowing north). Option A is the most tempting error — Mahanadi originates from Sihawa hills in Chhattisgarh, NOT Amarkantak, and Betwa rises in Raisen district. Option B (Tapi, Wainganga, Pench) originate from the Satpura ranges near Betul–Chhindwara, not Amarkantak. Option D rivers rise in the Vindhya-Bundelkhand belt.

questions.stem: The Kaleshwaram Lift Irrigation Scheme (KLIS) in Telangana — the world's largest lift irrigation project by installed pump capacity — draws water from the Godavari at the Medigadda barrage. At this barrage, the Godavari receives the discharge of which major tributary?

options.option_text: Pranahita river (confluence of Wardha and Wainganga rivers)
Manjira river (originating from Balaghat ranges in Maharashtra)
Indravati river (originating in Kalahandi, Odisha plateau)
Kinnerasani river (from Palvoncha forests of Telangana)

questions.explanation: Medigadda barrage sits at the confluence of the Pranahita and Godavari rivers. The Pranahita is itself formed by the merger of the Wardha and Wainganga rivers in Maharashtra's Gadchiroli district — making it the largest tributary of the Godavari by volume. Option B (Manjira) is a right-bank Godavari tributary that joins near Nizamabad, well upstream. Option C (Indravati) joins the Godavari further downstream in Chhattisgarh. Option D (Kinnerasani) is a much smaller Godavari tributary in Telangana's Bhadradri Kothagudem district.
